readiness.evidencePolicy: Generated documents and asserted decisions are design evidence only. Schema validation, mock tests, account plans and deployed-system tests require separate receipts tied to the exact configuration. This export does not ingest implementation evidence.

requirements.statement: Accept uploaded PDF invoices, asynchronously extract supplier, invoice date, total and currency, and persist results in a review queue. Proposed acceptance: show supporting evidence and expose incomplete extraction or processing failures for correction.
requirements.rationale: Makes the requested extraction observable and prevents incomplete or unsupported values from silently becoming accounting records.
requirements.basis: “Users upload PDF invoices. Extract the supplier, invoice date, total and currency into a review queue.” Source evidence and explicit failure states are engineering proposals.

requirements.statement: Permit accounting submission only after an authorized reviewer approves the exact result revision and delivery payload; changes invalidate that approval. Enforce reviewer permissions on the server and retain the approval and delivery history.
requirements.rationale: Prevents model output or a later edit from bypassing the user's required human approval.
requirements.basis: “A reviewer approves a result before it is sent to our existing accounting API.” Revision-bound approval and server authorization are proposed controls.

requirements.statement: Repeated delivery and worker recovery must not create duplicate accounting invoices. Persist stable operation and payload identities, require a qualified destination idempotency contract, and reconcile uncertain external outcomes before allowing another submission.
requirements.rationale: A timeout can occur after accounting accepts an invoice; blind retries can create duplicates even when the local queue deduplicates jobs.
requirements.basis: “Delivery can repeat; retries must not create duplicate invoices.” Durable operation identity and uncertain-outcome reconciliation are proposed engineering controls, supported by the supplied durable-approval-and-uncertain-outcome practice.

requirements.statement: Keep invoice documents and extracted data within Australia across application processing, model inference, storage and data-bearing operational/recovery copies. Qualify the existing accounting destination before transfer. Explicitly flag unverified regional service/model support and prohibit silent cross-border fallback.
requirements.rationale: Personal invoice data could leave Australia through inference, backups, logs or the existing accounting integration unless every processing path is qualified.
requirements.basis: “they may contain personal data” and “Keep documents and extracted data in Australia; flag unverified service availability.”

requirements.statement: Retain invoice originals and extraction audit history for 90 days. Implement scheduled cleanup and document deletion behavior for database records, object versions and backups; qualify the retention start event and residual recovery windows before claiming compliance.
requirements.rationale: Cleanup must include audit records and versioned originals; backup windows can prevent immediate erasure and need explicit acceptance.
requirements.basis: “Keep originals and extraction audit history for 90 days.”

requirements.statement: Accept PDF invoices up to 10,000,000 bytes and plan asynchronous capacity for approximately 500 uploads per day. Reject oversized uploads explicitly before parsing. Qualify capacity with representative PDFs and retry/recovery workloads; peak arrival rate and completion-time targets remain unspecified.
requirements.rationale: Enforcing upload bounds protects parsing resources; daily volume informs capacity without inventing peak traffic or a processing deadline.
requirements.basis: “PDF invoices up to 10 MB, around 500 per day”

requirements.statement: Persist workflow state and queued work transactionally with stable invoice/job identities. Bound retries, recover stalled workers and retain exhausted jobs in a visible dead-letter/recovery state. Restrict recovery to authorized operators, preserve identity and audit history, and test process interruption and retry exhaustion without losing work or bypassing approval.
requirements.rationale: Durable recovery prevents worker crashes and exhausted retries from losing invoices or creating new delivery identities. The PostgreSQL queue and recovery state are proposed internal engineering choices.
requirements.basis: “Use a durable job queue, stable invoice/job identity, bounded retries, a dead-letter/recovery path, approval checks and an idempotent outbound operation.”

requirements.statement: Reference the existing accounting system without provisioning or modifying it. Accept administrator-supplied endpoint and credentials through protected configuration. Implement and qualify authenticated payload mapping, destination idempotency and outcome reconciliation before delivery; exclude secrets from browser responses, model inputs and logs. Accounting data handling must satisfy the existing Australian residency requirement.
requirements.rationale: An external endpoint is not a verified integration. Qualification must establish safe delivery without expanding provisioning into the client's accounting system.
requirements.basis: “The accounting system already exists. An administrator will supply its endpoint and credentials; treat it as external, not a new system to provision.”
